correctness.rationale: For a connected height-two unicyclic poset, the radical basis is one arrow per comparability edge and all double-arrow products vanish. Every derivation is uniquely an edge-coefficient pair (beta_e,z_e), with rank matrix consisting of private beta pivots and signed incidence entries z. Inner derivations exactly have beta a vertex-potential gradient, i.e. signed cycle sum zero. In any prescribed nonzero cohomology class at least one cycle beta is nonzero; the zero-beta support is then a forest, whose signed incidence rows are independent over any characteristic. Hence rank is the number of nonzero edge pairs. Additive character orthogonality gives the cycle coefficient ((q²-1)^j-(-1)^j)/q times binomial(L,j), and independent off-cycle pairs multiply by (1+(q²-1)T)^(m-L). The rank-one coefficient is qL and all ranks 1..m occur. Independently enumerated pairs on isolated 4- and 6-cycles over q=2,3 with signed sum lambda=1, confirming all coefficients and totals q^(2L-1); rank-one counts 8,12,12,18 respectively.
residual_risks: No multiple cycles, nonfield rings, higher height or automorphism-twisted derivations covered.
